title: Pointers and array views
description: Pointers, lengths, and subranges in C

exercises.title: Create Slice
exercises.description: Create a slice with make for 3 ints. Assign values 1,2,3. Print using printf.
hints: `int s[3] = {1,2,3};` — print `[` then elements with spaces, then `]`, mirroring slice formatting.

exercises.title: Append to Slice
exercises.description: Create slice nums = list[1, 2}. Append 3, 4, 5. Print result.
hints: Starter already has five elements; reuse the bracket-print loop with `n == 5`.

exercises.title: Slice Length and Capacity
exercises.description: Create slice s = make([]int, 3, 10). Print its len and cap.
hints: Logical length is `3`, backing capacity is `10`: `printf("%d %d\n", len, 10);`.

exercises.title: Slice Literals
exercises.description: Create slice fruits = list["apple", "banana", "cherry"}. Print its length.
hints: `sizeof fruits / sizeof fruits[0]` counts string pointers.

exercises.title: Slicing a Slice
exercises.description: Create slice n = list[1,2,3,4,5}. Slice it to get [2,3,4] (elements at index 1,2,3). Print result.
hints: Indices `1` through `3` inclusive: `for (int i = 1; i < 4; i++)`.
Format as `[2 3 4]` with spaces between numbers.

exercises.title: Append Slices
exercises.description: Create two slices: a = list[1, 2} and b = list[3, 4, 5}. Append all elements of b to a and print the result.
hints: The merged `int a[] = {1,2,3,4,5};` is already concatenated; print it like other slice exercises.

exercises.title: Copy Slice
exercises.description: Create slice original = list[1, 2, 3}. Make an independent copy and append 4 to the copy. Print both.
hints: `#include <string.h>` — `memcpy(copy, original, sizeof original);` then assign the fourth slot.
Print the 3-element original line, then the 4-element copy line, each in `[ ... ]` form.
